transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I keep cutting people off and jumping into things before they’re finished talking or deciding, and it’s starting to mess up my job and my money. It's just getting really frustrating because I can't seem to stop myself, and it's causing a lot of stress both at work and with my wife.
Do you also feel physically restless or overly active, like you can’t sit still, fidget a lot, or are always on the go?

Yes, absolutely, it's like I have a motor inside me that never shuts off from the moment I wake up, and I can't even relax on my days off. My leg is always bouncing, I'm constantly drumming my fingers, and sitting through a meeting or dinner feels so unbearable that I have to keep popping up. When I'm stuck in traffic or waiting around, I get this awful crawling feeling inside and just have to move.
Before age 15, did you often get into fights, bully or threaten others, deliberately destroy property, steal, lie, or break serious rules like running away or staying out all night?
No, I don't recall doing those kinds of things at all. I was never getting into fights, stealing, or destroying property when I was a kid. I was just really hyper and had a hard time sitting still.
Did these problems with inattention, impulsivity, or restlessness start before age 12, and were they present in more than one setting such as home and school?

Yes, absolutely, it started way before I was 12, both at home and at school. Back in elementary school, I couldn't stay in my seat and was always blurting out answers, which got me constant notes home. My parents said my report cards were always full of comments about me being too "overactive" and "disruptive."
Do these attention, impulsivity, or restlessness symptoms still happen in several areas of your life now, such as at work, at home, and in social situations?

Yes, they definitely affect me everywhere, especially at work and at home. On the job, I'm getting safety write-ups, missing details on the line, and constantly interrupting my supervisors. At home, it causes a lot of tension with my wife because I talk over her, make impulsive money decisions, and can't even sit still through dinner.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a longstanding childhood-onset pattern of hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention occurring in multiple settings and causing clear occupational and marital impairment. Symptoms began before age 12, persisted into adulthood, and include interrupting others, blurting out answers, inability to sit still, constant motor restlessness, distractibility/missing details, and impulsive decisions. No history suggestive of conduct disorder was reported.
